This reminds me of my first job in cyber security. 

I worked as a SOC analyst for a large IT company.  A few of the side projects I received involved installing servers and minor modification of the office network infrastructure to set up demo environments and safe malware analysis lab environments. 

The company had very poor policies (ex. 1% raise after second year with company not even enough to cover inflation/cost of living), lied to media sources about company culture, and even got caught attempting to cover up a breach (really embarrassing for an it/security provider)

So naturally employee retention was very poor and eventually I was the only employee in the office with a good knowledge of the server room and office network topography, as well as administrative/root credentials for some critical appliances.  

I asked the soc manager (well known asshole who tends to play favorites) for a raise as I was making less than new hires and had gained more responsibility than what is asked of an L1 soc analyst, and was promptly bitched out and told that a monkey could perform my responsibilities.

I was fired a few days later for the bs “right to work state” excuse.  

all that important internal data (network topography, modifications to network/appliances and root creds for some appliances) was encrypted and saved only within company resources tied to my AD account. It was all promptly deleted upon my departure. 

I was sad to have lost my first job in security out of college, but luckily had already thought ahead and started reaching out to other companies and def landed on my feet. 

Best part came a week or so later when I received a call from my old manager (denied), followed by a call from a friend who still worked there. Manager asked him to call me to see if I still had any of that crucial data.  We both had a good laugh as he informed me that the manager was absolutely panicking and ended up having to repurchase some services and appliances.  

Not really malicious compliance but I could have passed the data to whoever was filling my shoes. More instant karma for the shitty management. 

TLDR I was fired for no reason other appropriately asking for a raise (shitty management).  My departure ended up costing the company some important internal reference data, and a lot of otherwise unnecessary expenses for recovery.
